messages:
sri: Heads-up — seeing steady memory growth when serving mistral-7b-base with long contexts (~24k-32k tokens). KV cache bytes climb over time and don't get reclaimed between sessions. Repro uses rope_scale=8192, single model shard, dedicated node.

anna: Can you paste the minimal repro and the runtime flags? Is this on dedicated or hosted? :eyes:

sri: Dedicated dev box (g4dn-like). Repro steps: start server, send a 28k token prompt (chunked), then do ~100 short followups. After each request `kv_cache_total_bytes` increases. No large active requests when it grows. Flags: `--rope-scale=8192 --kv-pool-sweep-interval=0 --kv-page-size=65536 --batching=enabled`

sri: Quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-02-21T14:22:10Z] kv: alloc_page id=12 size=65536 free=0 total_pages=128
[2026-02-21T14:22:15Z] kv: total_bytes=129843456 active_entries=2432
[2026-02-21T14:22:40Z] kv: total_bytes=134217728 active_entries=2548
[2026-02-21T14:23:10Z] kv: total_bytes=139591040 active_entries=2679
```
No `page_free` events observed.

mike: Hm. Two quick hypotheses: (1) shape mismatch across requests — if MQA/GQA settings differ between model instantiation and request kernel path we end up allocating distinct KV buffers; (2) batching heuristics producing many ephemeral caches/slots that never reconcile because keys differ by rope-scaled offsets. Can you dump per-layer kv shapes with `--log-kv-shapes`?

vlad: Mistral's relative-rope implementation with rope_scale != 1 can change the effective position encoding handling in the runtime. If the kernel selector treats that as a different "layout" for KV it may allocate a separate pool per rope bucket. Also check head/size packing: mismatched head counts (e.g., when using quantized model variant vs canonical) will cause different kernel choices and thus different alloc ids.

anna: Also check that `kv-pool-sweep-interval`==0 disables periodic reclamation — that could be the main culprit. If sweep is disabled we will never coalesce freed pages into global free lists. Why is that turned off in the repro?

sri: It was set to 0 to test whether the sweep itself was the cause. When I flip it back to 30s I still see growth but somewhat slower, not reclaimed to baseline.

mike: Please try two quick experiments: 
1) Force `--force-kv-shape=packed` (makes kernel selector unify shapes) and reproduce.
2) Run with `--batching-heuristic=seq_len_bucket` (coarse bucketing) to avoid tiny, unique seq_len batches.

vlad: Another internal note: we observed a similar pattern months ago where fragmentation increased because small page allocations (<=64k) accumulated. The GC doesn't compact across layers; it only frees whole pages back to OS when global free pages > threshold. If many pages are partially used they remain in per-shard free lists.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: related CI job #6283 shows 6% increase in steady-state memory for mistral long-context workloads since commit 9a7b2f8 (kv: change to per-request cache lifetime).

anna: Good catch, perf-bot. 6% matches what sri reported. sri — can you capture a heap profile (`pmap`/`smem`) and the runtime `--dump-kv-map` after a run? That will let us see fragmentation vs true leaks.

sri: Uploaded heap snap and kv-map to the thread: link (private). Quick kv-map snippet for layer 10:
```
layer_10: pages=[0,3,7,12,17,23,27,31] partial_used=[32768,49152,16384,65536,49152,32768,49152,16384]
free_pages_pool=2
```
Total pages high and many partially used -> points to fragmentation.

mike: If those partial_used numbers are dynamic due to differing sequence_lengths, we could improve reuse by implementing a small-size-slab per-page (coalesce small entries) or by forcing stricter reuse rules: prefer reusing pages with matching "bucket" of used bytes instead of only exact size.

vlad: Short-term mitigations: 
- re-enable sweep (interval 30s)
- set `--kv-max-pages=256` to bound growth and trigger eviction fallback (degrades perf but prevents OOM)
- set `--batching-heuristic=seq_len_bucket`

anna: Long-term: add logging to kernel selector to emit `(model_variant, head_count, qtype, rope_scale)` tag with each allocation id so we can attribute allocations to kernel variants. Also add a `kv_reuse_metric` showing reuse rate per page.

sri: Will open a tiny PR with additional telemetry + a debug endpoint to force a pool compact. For now I repro'd the same behavior with qwen-7b when rope_scale !=1 but less aggressively; Llama variants show a different pattern (more reuse) so seems model-specific.

mike: That pattern (qwen less aggressive) smells like GQA vs MQA handling in the model loader. Qwen often uses grouped attention which our kernel selector treats differently (creating extra buffers).

vlad: Filing follow-up ticket: INF-2142 "KV fragmentation: rope-scale variant allocations + kernel selector attribution". Assign to eng-runtime.

anna: Thanks. sri — please link PR/heap snaps. If someone oncall sees rising memory in prod, the short-term knob is `--kv-max-pages` + `--kv-pool-sweep-interval=30`. :thumbsup: 

sri: Will do, thx. I'll post the PR link once ready. :shipit:
